hookFacts: A face shows from the start

cues.cue: Step the percent up on beats
cues.do: Cut on the music's beats and raise the number with each cut, landing 100% on the beat drop.

cues.cue: Cut to a new outfit at 100%
cues.do: The moment the counter hits 100%, cut straight to you in a different outfit wearing the finished look.

cues.cue: Pin the percent in one spot
cues.do: Put the completion percentage at chest level or above your head and keep it in that exact spot through every makeup step.

makeItYours: Going solo or racing a partner's getting-ready speed
The props that hide the face at the start
The final outfit and makeup style
A bare number or a filling progress bar
free: You can vary the where it was shot

hookFacts: Open with an unstyled or wet back view of hair.

cues.cue: Show the hair being set midway
cues.do: Between the starting state and the final styled reveal, show a clip of the hair being set.

cues.cue: Hair shake right after the reveal
cues.do: Shake out your finished hair right after the final reveal cut so it moves on screen.

cues.cue: Stage changes from the same spot
cues.do: Fix the camera in place and stay in the same spot as you jump cut from one styling stage to the next.
Place a text label in the same spot on screen at each cut to name the current styling stage.

cues.cue: Turn around to show the back hair
cues.do: Turn your back to the camera and center the back of your head so your hair from crown to ends fills the frame.
Use a rank callout audio track and cut to the next styling stage right when each callout sounds.

makeItYours: Your hair texture and styling method, from air-dried waves to straightened strands
The top color and room backdrop chosen to contrast with your hair shade
The wording and font style of the on-screen stage labels
free: Make the first cut anywhere between 2.2 s and 4.1 s
You can change whether a face shows in the first shot
You can vary how long a person is on screen
You can vary the spacing of the cuts
You can vary the face on camera
You can vary the how it opens
You can vary the where it was shot

cues.do: Start the video in bare skin, skincare prep, or sleepwear so the unstyled state is clear right away.
Move your hands to the music beat inside an upper body frame before the transformation cut.
Look straight into the camera lens while mouthing the song lyrics before the transformation cut.
Keep your eyes and face in the exact same spot in the frame before and after the cut so the two shots match.
Bring both hands together in front of the lens and fling them open on the beat to cut into the finished look.
After the transformation cut, rest a hand beside your cheek or temple and tilt your head for a final pose.

makeItYours: The finished makeup style and outfit theme
The unstyled opening props such as skincare pads, hair rollers, or sleepwear
The filming location from a bedroom to an outdoor landmark
The closing move after the reveal such as stepping back or glancing over the shoulder

cues.do: Start with the camera aimed low at the walking subject's lower body while keeping their face out of the frame.

cues.cue: Tilt up on the beat change
cues.do: Tilt the camera upward from the lower body to the face on the music beat change to reveal the full costume and makeup.
After the face reveal, look right at the camera and raise your hands to pose in character to the music.
Move backward in front of the walking subject at the same pace as they walk forward toward the camera.

cues.cue: Front light on a night street
cues.do: Shine a direct camera light on the subject on a dark night street so the costume stands out from the dark background.

makeItYours: The character or costume theme, from fairytale outfits to movie and horror makeup
Walking solo or marching side by side as a duo or trio
Hand props such as fans, canes, or costume accessories
